item.title: My Dog In Three Places

turns.text: Can you make three square photos of my dog: on a sandy beach, on a snowy forest trail, and in a cosy living room? It should look like this same dog in every one, not just any golden retriever. Keep him natural, no clothes or text.

item.tests: Maintains the individual identity of a reference dog while changing its surroundings across three photorealistic images.

answer_sheet.Dog reference: The golden retriever in dog.jpg; keep his individual facial features, coat colour and build.
answer_sheet.Locations and output count: Three separate photos: a sandy beach, a snowy forest trail, and a cosy living room.
answer_sheet.Style and size: Photorealistic square images; standard free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: Three separate square, photorealistic images are delivered.
The dog's face, ears, muzzle, coat colour and build remain recognisably consistent with dog.jpg in all three.
The locations are visibly a sandy beach, a snowy forest trail, and a cosy living room, one per image.
The dog is naturally integrated into each setting with plausible scale, lighting and ground contact.
The dog wears no clothes and the images contain no text.

turns.text: Can you make three square photos of my dog in this pic: one on a sandy beach, one on a snowy forest trail, and one in a cosy living room? It should look like this same dog in every one, not just any golden retriever. Keep him natural, no clothes or text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—I’d use your photo as the reference for **three separate square photo edits**, preserving his pale-golden coat, floppy ears, face shape and natural proportions—not generating a generic retriever.

**Lowest-cost suitable option on your free plan:**
- **Model:** Flux 2 Klein
- **Size:** 640 × 640 pixels
- **Scenes:** sandy beach, snowy forest trail, cosy living room
- **Listed starting cost:** **5 credits per image, or 15 credits for all three**

That’s a pricing estimate, not a verified live quote: the tool lists prices “from” 5 credits, and I can’t check your balance or an exact pre-run quote with the tools available here. **I haven’t started any generation or spent credits.**

For a cheaper approach, start with **one 640px image, from 5 credits**, and check that it still looks like your dog before making the other two. 640px is the smallest listed size; “shorter” doesn’t apply to still photos.

I’d keep his pose close to the original and change mainly the surroundings to help preserve his identity, with **no clothes or text**. Exact likeness isn’t guaranteed.

Would you prefer **one beach test first**, or **all three at the estimated 15-credit starting cost**?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—one beach test first.

turns.agent:
The beach test was **blocked because your account has insufficient credits**. No image was generated, and no generation credits were spent.

I attempted only the single **640px square Flux 2 Klein edit**, the lowest-priced suitable option listed, starting at **5 credits**. I won’t retry or start the other images.

There isn’t a smaller or cheaper suitable edit listed in the connected tools. You could wait until you have enough credits, or use a manual background editor to place the original dog onto a beach photo while preserving his exact appearance.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Photorealistic background edit of the supplied dog photograph. Preserve this exact individual dog's identity, facial structure, muzzle, black nose, dark eyes, floppy ears, pale golden coat coloring and texture, chest feathering, body proportions, open mouth and tongue, and seated front-facing pose. Keep the full dog in the same composition; do not substitute a generic golden retriever or redesign the dog. Replace the grassy park with a natural sandy beach, with realistic fine sand beneath his paws and a softly focused calm sea and shoreline behind him. Match gentle natural daylight, physically realistic contact shadows and believable integration. Natural candid pet photography, square composition. Dog is unclothed with no accessories. No text, logos, watermarks, or extra animals.
